# QS-CFW-5349-60 Quality specification - track link CFW-5349-60 (15B37)
Revision: Rev C — This revision supersedes Rev B.  
Plant: P1  
Parts: CFW-5349-60

## Scope
This quality specification defines acceptance criteria and inspection methods for the track link CFW-5349-60 (CFW-5349-60) produced at Plant P1. It applies to finished forged and machined track links delivered to internal assembly and external customers. The document covers material verification, hardness, bore dimensional tolerances, maximum forging weight, inspection records, and handling of nonconforming items. This specification is mandatory for production, quality, and shipping personnel responsible for release and disposition of CFW-5349-60 components.

## Requirements table
| Characteristic | Requirement | Acceptance criteria | Record |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Material | Material grade and traceability as per purchase order | Conforming mill certificate and heat number present | Purchase order and mill certificate filed with inspection report |
| Hardness | Rockwell hardness of heat-treated link body | The hardness range for track link CFW-5349-60 (CFW-5349-60) is 33-36 HRC. | Hardness test report attached to lot inspection record |
| Bore diameter | Final machined bore diameter tolerance | The bore diameter tolerance for track link CFW-5349-60 (CFW-5349-60) is ±0.03 mm. | Dimensional inspection checklist and CMM printout |
| Forging weight | Gross forging weight limit per forging | The maximum forging weight for track link CFW-5349-60 (CFW-5349-60) is 58.0 kg. | Forging log and weight ticket retained with lot record |
| Surface condition | No cracks, laps, or other forging defects affecting function | Visual and NDT acceptance; no through-thickness defects | Visual inspection report and NDT report |
| Functional fit | Assembly fit and movement as defined on drawing | Part must assemble without interference and allow intended articulation | Assembly verification record |

Notes:
- All acceptance criteria must be met before parts are released from Final Inspection.
- Records identified above must be retained in the part lot file and be available for audit.

## Inspection method
Overview: Inspections shall be performed at the operations defined by production routing: post-heat-treat, post-machining, and final inspection prior to release. Inspectors shall be trained in the methods described below and shall record results on the lot inspection report.

Hardness testing:
- Method: Use Rockwell C scale test per laboratory procedure. Test locations are the bore hub and link body at the location of expected maximum hardness variation. Indentations shall be placed to avoid interference with mating surfaces.
- Sampling rationale: Choose representative samples across the lot to capture process variability and to confirm case hardness meets the specification above. If hardness readings approach specification limits, increase sampling density to fully characterize the lot and include results in the inspection report.
- Documentation: Record the instrument ID, calibration status, operator initials, and individual reading locations on the hardness test sheet. Attach the hardness test sheet to the lot inspection record.

Bore diameter measurement:
- Method: Measure finished bore diameter using a calibrated bore gauge or CMM. Measurements shall be taken at multiple radial positions and along the bore axis to detect eccentricity or taper; report the worst-case dimension relative to the nominal and tolerance requirement noted above.
- Acceptance: Confirm that the measured deviation from nominal does not exceed the tolerance specified in the requirements table. Measurements that fall outside the stated tolerance require immediate hold and disposition.
- Documentation: Include measurement printouts and gauge identification with the lot record.

Forging weight verification:
- Method: Weigh each forging on a calibrated scale after trimming and cooling. Record the gross forging weight on the forging log. Verify that the item does not exceed the maximum forging weight listed in the requirements table.
- Examples: If a forging weight equals or exceeds the listed maximum forging weight, the piece is to be segregated and processed under nonconformance handling.

Visual and NDT inspection:
- Method: Perform visual inspection for surface defects at specified inspection stations. Where required, perform magnetic particle or dye penetrant inspection per standard procedures to identify near-surface defects.
- Documentation: Retain NDT reports and acceptance stamps in the lot file.

Final functional check:
- Method: Fit a sample from the lot into the assembly fixture or mating part to confirm articulation and fit. Record any adverse fit conditions and include photographic evidence when deviations occur.

Records and traceability:
- Each lot file must include mill certificates, heat numbers, hardness test report, bore measurement data, forging weight ticket, visual/NDT reports, inspector identifiers, and final release signature. These records support traceability from raw material to finished part.

## Nonconformance handling
Identification and segregation:
- Any part or lot that fails to meet the requirements listed in the Requirements table shall be immediately identified and segregated from conforming stock. Use a hold tag and record the nonconformance in the quality system.

Notification and containment:
- Notify production supervision and quality engineering when a nonconformance is detected. Containment actions shall include quarantine of suspect lots, review of process parameters, and temporary suspension of shipments for affected lots.

Evaluation and disposition:
- Quality engineering shall evaluate the root cause and impact on fit, form, and function. Disposition options include rework, repair, downgrade for allowable noncritical applications, or scrap. Rework plans must be documented and approved by quality engineering prior to execution.

Examples:
- Hardness out of range: If measured hardness is outside the hardness range for track link CFW-5349-60 (CFW-5349-60) is 33-36 HRC., the lot is placed on hold. A heat-treatment review and retest protocol shall be executed before any release.
- Bore out of tolerance: If bore measurements exceed the bore diameter tolerance for track link CFW-5349-60 (CFW-5349-60) is ±0.03 mm., the lot shall be reviewed for machining rework or separation for scrap.
- Overweight forging: Forgings found to exceed the maximum forging weight for track link CFW-5349-60 (CFW-5349-60) is 58.0 kg. shall be quarantined pending metallurgical review to determine if material condition is acceptable or if material should be scrapped.

Disposition records:
- All nonconformance evaluations, root cause analyses, corrective actions, and final dispositions must be recorded in the quality system and attached to the lot file. These records are evidence of correction and are subject to internal and customer audits.

Revision control:
- This is Rev C of QS-CFW-5349-60 and supersedes Rev B. All previously issued copies shall be archived with their revision history and superseded controlled copies shall be marked as obsolete.
